blocks.text: You can connect your GitHub organization to Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance to gain continuous visibility and governance for third-party apps installed in the GitHub environment.
A user with an Organization Owner role in the relevant GitHub organization is required to connect 3rd-Party App Governance to your GitHub organization.
To connect your GitHub organization to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: Click Connect in the upper-right corner of the App Dashboard.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: From the drop-down menu, select GitHub.

blocks.text: See image.
The Add Integration window appears.

blocks.item: In the Add Integration window, click Add.

blocks.text: See image.
You are redirected to the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

blocks.item: Enter the tenant details and complete the configuration steps required for adding a new SaaS application tenant. To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

blocks.text: The Add SaaS Application Tenant page closes after successful addition of the new tenant. After a connection is achieved, it might take a while to pull and ingest all relevant application data depending on the size of your tenant. During this time, a message displays indicating that the integration is still being processed. After integration is completed, a success message appears, and the tenant details are updated on the Settings page. You then receive an email from Zscaler when the integration is ready for further review.
You can view the list of added tenants along with information such as integration status, enabled features, first connected time, last synced time, etc. on the Settings page.
You might need to reconnect GitHub to 3rd-Party App Governance if an error displays (e.g., Grant Expired). To reconnect GitHub to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Reconnect icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.
A consent window appears. After consent is granted, the connection is updated.
The Reconnect option is available only for legacy tenants. The existing tenants onboarded via the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal are called legacy tenants.
You can edit a GitHub connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To edit a GitHub connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Edit icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: You are redirected to the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

blocks.item: Edit the tenant details as required and click Save.

blocks.text: The connection is updated. The Add SaaS Application Tenant page closes after a successful update.
You can delete a GitHub connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To delete a GitHub connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Delete icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.
The following step is not required for legacy connections.
You are redirected to the SaaS Application Tenants page in the Zscaler Admin Console, where a confirmation window appears.
The connection is deleted. The SaaS Application Tenants page closes after successful deletion.
The following table lists the permissions and data collected after integration:

table: Read-only access to organization membership, organization projects, and team membership
Grants read access to a user's email addresses
Grants read access to the audit log data
